Maria: RFC follow-up: cross-region credit reconciliation. We need a clear protocol for when regional brokers diverge (eg due to network partition) so fairness doesn't break. Draft options below.

Takashi: TL;DR options?

Maria: 3 options: 1) Strong leader per tenant (single region) with sync writes; 2) Conflict-free counters (CRDT-like) with periodic anti-entropy; 3) Lease-based tokens with short-lived global lease and local optimistic ops.

Noor: Leader gives correctness but big latency and HA complexity. CRDT approach seems elegant but might overcount in merges.

Maria: Exactly. CRDT monotonic counters need careful tombstone/decay logic to avoid permanent over-allocation. Lease approach: give local brokers ephemeral lease for slices of tenant quota; leases auto-expire. During partition, local brokers can continue using leased slice.

Takashi: Lease model sounds pragmatic: shards by tenant -> small leases reduce blast radius. How do we refill leases?

Maria: Refill via background reconcile: central allocator periodically redistributes unused capacity. Reconcile uses idempotent ops and vector timestamps to detect stale leases.

Noor: What about abuse: attacker could hold many small leases across regions. Need global abuse detector that can reduce effective available capacity per org and revoke leases fast.

Maria: Yes we plan revoke API + push-based revocation channel. Also a fast failover: if reconcile detects gross divergence, edges go into conservative local-admit mode (smaller token grants) until fixed.

infra-bot: Ops note: implement metrics: cross-region divergence count, lease-revocation-rate, reconcile-latency, and fraction of requests served from stale leases. Add runbook for reconcile failures.

Takashi: Implementation spike idea: prototype lease allocator backed by redis cluster with TTL semantics and a reconcile job. Measure p99 on lease-grant path and reconcile cost.

Noor: Also add audit trail for lease grants and revocations (PII-free). Retention 90d.

Maria: Decisions for RFC update: prefer lease-based with optional strong-leader override for sensitive tenants, include revoke channel and conservative fail-open policy, add metrics and runbook. Action: Takashi will run prototype spike; Noor will draft revoke API and telemetry.

sre-bot: Reminder: mTLS for revoke channel and auth checks on revoke requests.

Maria: Thanks all. Will update RFC with chosen design and add checklist for canary.
